item.title: Mod Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
I'm sorry if I have no familiarity with the Bosnian war the Balkan MTF (is that an already existing MTF or is it a new one you made for this skip?) or what Balkan is.

Hey blazerboy69420. As someone with a bit more familiarity with the Bosnian War, a lot of your critique here is fairly oblivious to how this story fits in to the themes and conflicts of the war. That time period in former Yugoslavia is famous for a heightened sense of nationalism and disapora, so things like ethnic Croats being born in Canada (thereby not having as direct a connection to Croatia itself), and a bar where ethnicity is not a characteristic one might be killed for are, quite frankly, very salient to the story that's trying to be told here.

Furthermore, a story structure similar to Life is Strange is not uncommon nor something that necessarily needs to be knocked here.

Do you think the Chaos Insurgency just goes recruiting for agents on the fly? Sure I guess the mission stuff would cause a lot of animosity between Sam and Kosta but the fact that Sam somehow joined the CI because of it is literally so unrealistic, not just in-universe but irl. If you're working for the Foundation and you hear there's a splinter group that is actively engaging in attacks on the Foundation, who's firepower and military strength is larger than some countries, and they're actively terminating members of the CI as well, I wouldn't think twice of burying the possibility of me joining the CI to the ground.

The author is in sole control of the story they are telling here. If their conception of the CI is a strapped-for-manpower insurgent group that is desperate for members and is quick to recruit, then they are free to write that, so long as it makes sense in the setting and is sufficiently justified. You are also missing some pretty clear parallels here between the Foundation/CI and US allies/ insurgent groups during the Bosnian War.

If you're reading a pitch that is heavily mired in things you do not understand or have familiarity with, consider not critiquing them if you don't feel you are knowledgeable about the subject.

item.title: Re: A Balkan fairy tail
item.content:encoded:
Since no one else decided to crit this I guess I will.

+ show block
– hide block

The story is set in the Bosnian war. A girl with powers of a fairy is found in Bosnia. The Balkan MTF force captures her.

I'm sorry if I have no familiarity with the Bosnian war the Balkan MTF (is that an already existing MTF or is it a new one you made for this skip?) or what Balkan is. Also, what do you mean by "powers of a fairy", can you elaborate?

Agent Kosta, an ethnic Croat born in Canada is sent to recover her but the Balkan base is attacked by the Chaos insurgency. The battle ends with Kosta and one insurgent as the only survivors. Kosta grabs the girl and they go through the war-torn Bosnia, trying to reach the Croatian coast while running from the still alive insurgent.

A Croat born in Canada? You can just say she has Croat ethnicity ya know, don't need to use more words than you need to or just generally unimportant info.

So MTF Balkan has a base? I don't really think MTF's have their own proper bases, remember these guys are a Mobile Task Force, they move around a lot when needed to, not sure why they would have a central base.

I'm getting some big Life Is Strange 2 vibes, a normal human-being running away with a person that has extra-ordinary abilities to evade capture or worse. And didn't you just say that Kosta was the only survivor but now you're saying they're running away with the kid?

As they drive through Bosnia, Kosta starts to bond with the kid. The child doesn't speak but communicates with Kosta by creating pictures on the various surfaces with her fairy dust. They meet various individuals from all three sides of the Bosnian conflict.

Yeah, I'm getting more Life Is Strange 2 vibes from this, they meet people on their journey, some helpful and some not. By the way, I see no reason for the fairy dust scene being described here, remember the central narrative goes over the main story beats and what you intend on going for, not a 1-1 synopsis of every minute plot detail.

In an abandoned coffy bar "Amsterdam", where all of the ethnicities laugh and drink together, while the girl, now going by the name Bojana Skadaric, plays with the other kids, he gets drunk and tells the sad fate of his wife, and how he lost her in a mission. His best friend Sam blamed him for her loss and they never saw each other again.

Ok, this is where I'm gonna start to nitpick further. If you're trying to go for a sense of peace and serenity with this, I get what you're trying to do, but the whole "all ethnicities" thing just feels a bit forced and shoved in there to show for it? Don't take this as me being blatantly offensive or something because I'm truly NOT trying to come off like that, I don't know it just feels a bit out of touch and cliche. It kind of just comes off as your version of "I can just show peace and harmony by plopping a bunch of diverse characters with different ethnicities, religions, and sexual orientations all in one place getting along!"

Why did the girl's name change? Why didn't she share or have a name before? Is it because she was previously an inhabitant of the forest that can not be named?

Are they a he or a she? I'm just gonna call them Bojana. So Bojana is a kid..but gets drunk and mourns their wife..in front of the other kids? Why is this whole mission subplot even here or mentioned? It doesn't add anything to the story or the anomaly.

The insurgent attacks the pub and destroys it. They reach an area controlled by a Croatian warlord "Swedish" that commands a volunteer division while the local official army unwillingly follows his orders. Swedish is in a blood feud with a local Serbian warlord. He finds out about the fairy abilities of the girl, as she intervened in an execution, but before he could capture her the Serbs start an offensive and the Serbian commander challenges Swedish to come out.

Yeah I highly doubt a sole CI could wipe out an entire hub with a fairy in it, let alone destroy the ENTIRE pub, we're talking about one guy here. On to the Swedish stuff, "commands a volunteer division while the local official army unwillingly follow his orders", so basically a militia made up of civilians and corrupt army officials? That's probably a better and simpler way to describe it.

I don't know what to say about the rest, we'll see.

Enraged, Swedish leads the volunteers to battle. The leader of the official army realises that his commander went completely insane, and orders the evacuation of the village.

I still have no idea what to say, can't bite on this.

Kosta and Bojana go to the evacuation truck and are stoped by the voice of the chaos insurgent who calls Kosta by name, it is Sam. As he leaves to confront his former friend he tells the army leader to go far away with Bojana. He and Sam have only one bullet each and as they fire at each other a bomb drops between them, ending the footage.

…This just sounds so underwhelming and cliche. Do you think the Chaos Insurgency just goes recruiting for agents on the fly? Sure I guess the mission stuff would cause a lot of animosity between Sam and Kosta but the fact that Sam somehow joined the CI because of it is literally so unrealistic, not just in-universe but irl. If you're working for the Foundation and you hear there's a splinter group that is actively engaging in attacks on the Foundation, who's firepower and military strength is larger than some countries, and they're actively terminating members of the CI as well, I wouldn't think twice of burying the possibility of me joining the CI to the ground.

WHY HAS THIS ENTIRE ORDEAL EVEN BEEN RECORDED, HOW WOULD THIS LOOK IN THE ARTICLE, WHY IS THIS BEING CONTAINED AS ANOMALY WHEN IT'S LITERALLY JUST REGULAR FOUND FOOTAGE ABOUT A FAIRY

I can't bite on any of this.


tl;dr: I feel as though this is severely lacking in plot, there's incredibly cliche tropes in here, things that make 0 sense, and a feeling of more to be desired (and not in the good way).

I'm sorry if this sounds a bit vehement, I just wanted to be as honest and helpful as possible, since English probably isn't your first language I understand if that's why there were grammatical and wording errors. Have a good one.

item.title: A Balkan fairy tail
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History

Page Layout (Optional): The article is made out of several camera and audio footages.

Elevator Pitch: The story is set in the Bosnian war. A girl with powers of a fairy is found in Bosnia. The Balkan MTF force captures her. Agent Kosta, an ethnic Croat born in Canada is sent to recover her but the Balkan base is atacked by the Chaos insurgency. The battle ends with Kosta and one insurgent as the only survivors. Kosta grabs the girl and they go through the war torn Bosnia, trying to reach the Croatian coast while runing from the still alive insurgent.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: As they drive through Bosnia, Kosta starts to bond with the kid. The child doesn't speak but communicates with Kosta by creating pictures on the various surfaces with her fairy dust. They meet various individuals from all three sides of the Bosnian conflict. In an abandoned coffy bar "Amsterdam", where all of the ethnicities laugh and drink together, while the girl, now going by the name Bojana Skadaric, plays with the other kids, he gets drunk and tells the sad fate of his wife, and how he lost her in a mission. His best friend Sam blamed him for her loss and they never saw each other again. The insurgent atacks the pub and destroys it. They reach an area controled by a Croatian warlord "Swedish" that commands a volunteer division while the local offical army unwillingly follows his orders. Swedish is in a blood feud with a local Serbian warlord. He finds out about the fairy abilities of the girl, as she intervened in an execution, but before he could capture her the Serbs start an offensive and the Serbian commander challenges Swedish to come out. Enraged, Swedish leads the volunteers to battle. The leader of the official army realises that his commander went completely insane, and orders the evacuation of the village. Kosta and Bojana go to the evacuation truck and is stoped by the voice of the chaos insurgent who calls Kosta by name, it is Sam. As he leaves to confront his former friend he tells the army leader to go far away with Bojana. He and Sam have only one bulet each and as they fire at each other a bomb drops between them, ending the footage.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is about old conflicts that were never resolved coming to light. Bojana represents a generation not bound to those conflicts and has a future that she can choose freely, while Kosta, Sam and the people of Bosnia are chained to their fate.
